title: The Adventures of Sam Spade
identity_notes: Hard-boiled detective series built around Dashiell Hammett’s Sam Spade, with a more comic and self-aware radio characterization. The frozen GRH set is a surviving-subset archive, not a complete 245-broadcast run, and contains two proven duplicate-audio metadata conflicts.

eras.label: NBC Steve Dunne revival
eras.notes: Twenty-four-program sustained revival after a short hiatus.

historical_context.title: Network migration from ABC to CBS to NBC
historical_context.description: The program moved from the 1946 ABC summer series to a CBS regular run and then NBC, with a later sustained NBC revival.

historical_context.title: Postwar hard-boiled detective boom
historical_context.description: Sam Spade helped define the postwar radio private-eye style while adding more comedy and self-awareness than the literary version.

historical_context.title: Sam Spade character-rights litigation
historical_context.description: Warner Bros. challenged the radio use of the Sam Spade character; the dispute continued beyond the radio series.

historical_context.title: 1950 Red Channels controversy and cast/sponsor break
historical_context.description: Howard Duff and Dashiell Hammett were caught in the anti-Communist broadcasting climate; specialist histories connect the controversy to the end of the Duff/Wildroot era, while other accounts dispute a single direct cause for sponsor cancellation.
